newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Chance gasoline stock drop seen in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Chance gasoline stock drop seen in APIs.

text.p: Most traders expect this evening's weekly oil inventory report by the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a slight build in gasoline stocks, but refiner de-stocking and strong demand could lead to a surprise decline.
"There is a chance for a decent draw. Some may be letting winter inventories go down since prices are low," said Chevron Corp analyst Pat Hughes.
A consensus of trader estimates anticipates a build in gasoline stocks of 875,000 barrels in the API data.
Refiners tend to unwind winter grade gasoline inventories to make room for summer grade, used when demand is strongest.

Plus, a drop in gasoline prices has created a window to liquidate before producing the new grade which usually carries a premium. But, gasoline stock estimates ranged from a draw of two million barrels to a build of two million, as some traders expect increased imports from Europe to have boosted stocks.

"There is talk of higher imports, but there is a potential for unchanged to slightly down (gasoline stocks) because most of the talk centers around the gasoline arriving this week," said New York trader.
Tuesday's data reflects the week ended February 28.

Although gasoline demand is typically poor in February, implied demand the week before last was about eight million barrels per day (bpd), strong for any time of year. That demand followed a firm 7.7 million (bpd) the week before.
Dealers said the seasonal trough in gasoline demand bottomed in the first week in February when it hit 6.7 million bpd, the lowest level in about two years.
"The production side is still limited by maintenance," Chevron's Hughes said, noting gasoline output is still restrained by winter refinery maintenance.

Refineries have, slowly but surely, been emerging from seasonal repairs. Traders expect that refinery utilization rate will have risen about 0.5 percentage point from 88.8 percent, still making it below 90 percent.
Meanwhile, higher imports were seen boosting crude stocks between one and four million barrels, retaining the year-over-year crude stock surplus.

Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, were expected to drop a seasonal one to two million barrels. Refiners tend to cut distillate output as the winter draws to a close due to tapering heating oil demand.
